description: Recomputes MFM's long-term part of a price with the premium and the growth chosen by the user, with the same rule and bounds as the calculator of /en/top-down-bottom-up/#formula. Give exactly one of company (MFM company id: its owner earnings; counts as one company page of the account quota, nothing more if that company was already read today) or market (US, EU, JP, CA, CH: the net income of the basket's companies, the published bottom-up route; no quota). erp and x are fractions (0.04 = 4%, 0.01 = 1 point); defaults 4% and 0; out-of-range values are refused. Owner earnings, the payable share q, the return on equity, growth g and the spreads are measured and fixed. The result moves toward the market price but never past it. Optional sector (with market, US today: the sectors published in the sector table of /en/top-down-bottom-up/, by id such as information-technology or by name): the same calculation starting from that sector's published long-term part ÷ price and the market's parameters, plus the table of all the sectors of the market at the chosen erp and x; no live_price for a sector. Optional live comparison: live_price (company: price per share in the price currency; index or ETF: also month_end_price of the same instrument on MFM's price month). Optional own top-down (market or sector, never a company): own_pe, or own_earnings with own_index_level, for own_month (YYYY-MM), or own_series (up to 24 months): index earnings or P/E that the user's AI fetched from the provider the user chose (as reported, operating, exchange statistics, factsheet trailing P/E with or without negative earnings: its terms of use are the user's responsibility; MFM does not supply index earnings). Returns, per month, the long-term part ÷ index level with MFM's K of that month (or the chosen erp and x, applied equally to MFM's bottom-up), MFM's bottom-up of the same month, the gap between the two (a ratio of earnings: the same at every erp and x) and, for a market, its position against MFM's declared band (whole percent: the month's value, the typical value = median of the last 60 months, and their lowest and highest). State the earnings period: the comparison is meaningful on the same reporting period. Provisional months (official company prices not public yet: gap in whole percent only, no level) are never the starting point: a market reply starts from the latest month with official prices and gives the provisional months after it apart in provisional_months (gap, typical and largest error in percentage points, date by which the official prices are expected). Nothing is stored. The long-term part is dated, not real time. Descriptive only, never advice.

company.description: MFM company id, as in /en/company/<id>/ (e.g. aapl)

erp.description: Equity risk premium chosen by the user, fraction (default 0.04; range in the parameter file)

live_price.description: Live price fetched by the AI itself (optional), same unit and currency as MFM's price

market.description: Index or state with a published bottom-up long-term part

month_end_price.description: Index or ETF only: close of the same instrument on MFM's price month end, from the same source as live_price

own_earnings.description: Own top-down: index earnings per index unit (twelve months) from a provider chosen by the user; needs own_index_level

own_index_level.description: Own top-down: index level the earnings refer to (same provider, same month end)

own_month.description: Own top-down: month end (YYYY-MM) of own_pe or own_earnings/own_index_level; MFM's K and bottom-up of that month are used

own_pe.description: Own top-down (needs market, optionally sector): trailing index P/E from a provider chosen by the user, at the month end own_month

own_period_end.description: Own top-down (optional): last reporting period covered by the user's earnings (YYYY-MM), for the same-period check

own_series.description: Own top-down: a short monthly list instead of one month

sector.description: Sector of the market (needs market), id or English name as in the sector table, e.g. information-technology or Health care

x.description: Growth above the 10-year government bond rate, fraction (default 0; range in the parameter file)
